opportunities.title: APEX Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record and proven ability to lead collaborative work; must hold a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award, have teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved, and be based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Up to two Co-applicants based in UK research organisations covering a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: APEX Awards (Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research) offer established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary, curiosity-driven research across the boundary between science, engineering, and the social sciences and humanities. Partnership of the British Academy, Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering, supported by the Leverhulme Trust. Awards of up to £200,000 for up to 24 months, starting between 1 Oct and 31 Dec 2027.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; prior British Academy funding not required; some prior public engagement experience expected. Previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: A public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences. Awards of up to £8,000 for projects delivered in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or a performing arts organisation. Projects run between 1 April 2027 and 31 December 2028.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany. Applications evaluated on research interest in the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', commitment to interdisciplinary engagement, and potential for career development.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career scholars in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium in partnership with the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future'. The symposium takes place 21-23 April 2027 and covers travel, accommodation and visa costs, with seed funding available for international collaborations.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC; three-year award

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals (regardless of where doctorate obtained), or anyone with a doctorate from a UK university, or those demonstrating strong prior association with the UK. Viva completed between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Must not have been appointed to a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: A three-year, non-renewable Fellowship for outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards a significant piece of publishable research, funded by DSIT. Tenable from Autumn 2027 at a UK-based university or HEI.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based Higher Education Institution or Independent Research Organisation that will continue for the full duration of the award.
opportunities.summary: Awards to promote the acquisition and advancement of skills (e.g. quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages) by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination. Awards of up to £10,000 held for 6-12 months, commencing between 1 and 31 March 2027.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: up to £300,000 over 2 years (80% FEC; total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute holding an established role lasting the duration of the award, of postdoctoral or above status, spending at least 20% of their time on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants required; collaboration across disciplines required.
opportunities.summary: International interdisciplinary research projects led by and grounded in the humanities and/or social sciences, working with international partners across SHAPE and STEM disciplines, on the theme of Mobilities. Awards of up to £300,000 over 2 years, beginning March/April 2027.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: up to £150,000 for 12 months (Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences. Applications invited in areas including Security/Defence/Resilience, Indo-European Relations, Technology and AI, and Strategy-Making in Europe.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships enable UK-based early- and mid-career researchers to develop skills, networks and careers in the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors, embedded in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin. Up to two one-year fellowships of up to £150,000, commencing by September 2027.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available to current British Academy award-holders on any scheme, or applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award within the next six months (who must meet the eligibility for the scheme they intend to apply for).
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require, in addition to the amount already requested for research expenses, e.g. equipment to overcome barriers for disabled researchers, assistance for sensory impairment, caring costs for research trips, or support to make an application. Reviewed on a rolling, case-by-case basis.

opportunities.title: British Academy/Leverhulme Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to postdoctoral scholars (or equivalent) ordinarily resident in the UK. Applications require approval of the employing institution. Independent scholars may apply. Co-applicants may be from anywhere in the world, but the Principal Applicant must be ordinarily resident in the UK.
opportunities.summary: The British Academy's most popular scheme, providing awards of up to £10,000 tenable for up to 24 months to cover expenses arising from a defined research project. Funded as a public-private partnership including DSIT, Leverhulme Trust and Wellcome Trust. Applications for less than £500 not considered.
